text:
Tommy Novak has been handed the best seat in Pittsburgh: with Bryan Rust out, he has moved up beside Sidney Crosby and Rickard Rakell. It's a reward for a quiet, efficient start (12 points in 16 games, goals in back-to-back games against Montreal and Vegas), and it comes with the Penguins winless in four and Rakell in the trade rumors.

The process supports the promotion. Pittsburgh's expected-goal share is a little better with him on at five on five, and Evolving-Hockey had him in the 96th percentile among forwards last season for driving offense once teammates and opponents are accounted for. One caution: the Penguins have scored nearly four more goals than their chances deserved with him on the ice, so his assists have had some help. Not everyone is sold. Ryan Wilson of Hockey Hot Stove posted, "I'd rather Malkin than Novak on the power play." Next to Crosby, his job is simple: move the puck and keep the chances coming.
headline: Moving up beside Crosby
